question: According to the manual, what percentage of motorcycle crashes result in head or neck injury?
choice_a: About one out of every five motorcycle crashes
choice_b: About one out of every fifty motorcycle crashes
choice_d: Head and neck injuries are extremely rare in motorcycle crashes
explanation: The manual states that one out of every five motorcycle crashes results in head or neck injuries, and that these injuries account for a majority of serious and fatal injuries to motorcyclists.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.5, 'Helmet Use'

question: Helmeted riders involved in a crash are how much more likely to survive head injuries compared to unhelmeted riders?
choice_b: Three times more likely to survive head injuries
choice_c: Exactly the same likelihood either way
choice_d: Twice as likely to suffer additional injuries
explanation: The manual states that helmeted riders are three times more likely to survive head injuries than those not wearing helmets at the time of a crash.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.5, 'Helmet Use'

question: A study of more than 900 motorcycle crashes, in which 40% of riders wore helmets, found what about DOT-compliant helmets and peripheral vision?
choice_a: Helmets blocked side vision in nearly half the crashes studied
choice_b: The study could not draw any conclusion about vision
choice_c: It did not find even one case where a helmet kept a rider from spotting danger to the side
choice_d: Helmets improved vision only at night
explanation: The manual cites this study to rebut the belief that helmets limit peripheral vision -- a DOT-compliant helmet lets you see as far to the sides as necessary, and the study found no case of a helmet preventing a rider from spotting danger.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.5, 'Helmet Use'

question: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips of what length, and at what point in the ride?
choice_a: Long trips of over 100 miles, near the end of the ride
choice_b: Trips to and from work, during the final mile home
choice_c: Highway trips of at least 30 minutes at highway speed
choice_d: Short trips of less than five miles, just a few minutes after starting out
explanation: The manual states that most crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles, just a few minutes after starting out.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.5, 'Helmet Use'

question: Most riders are traveling at what speed when a crash occurs, and what effect does a helmet have at that speed?
choice_a: Slower than 30 mph; at these speeds helmets can cut both the number and severity of head injuries by half
choice_b: Faster than 60 mph; helmets have little effect at that speed
choice_c: Exactly the posted speed limit; helmets have no measurable effect
choice_d: Slower than 10 mph; helmets are unnecessary at such low speeds
explanation: Most riders are riding slower than 30 mph when a crash occurs, and at these speeds helmets can cut both the number and the severity of head injuries by half.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.5, 'Helmet Use'

question: What two primary types of helmets does the manual describe, based on the level of coverage they provide?
explanation: The manual describes two primary types of helmets, providing two different levels of coverage: three-quarter and full face.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.6, 'Helmet Selection'

question: Whichever helmet style a rider chooses, what should the rider make sure of to get the most protection?
choice_a: It matches the color of the motorcycle
choice_b: It is at least five years old to be properly broken in
choice_c: It is DOT- and state-compliant, fits snugly all the way around, and has no obvious defects such as cracks, loose padding or frayed straps
choice_d: It is as lightweight as possible, regardless of certification
explanation: The manual advises checking that a helmet is designed to meet DOT and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no obvious defects such as cracks, loose padding or frayed straps.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.6, 'Helmet Selection'

question: A label from what organization gives added assurance of a helmet's quality, beyond DOT compliance?
explanation: The manual notes that helmets with a label from the Snell Memorial Foundation also give riders an assurance of quality, in addition to DOT compliance.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.6, 'Helmet Selection'

question: What does the manual say about a windshield or eyeglasses as substitutes for a faceshield or goggles?
choice_a: A windshield is not a substitute for a faceshield or goggles, and most windshields, eyeglasses, or sunglasses will not protect eyes from wind
choice_b: A windshield fully replaces the need for eye protection
choice_c: Sunglasses provide better wind protection than goggles
choice_d: Eyeglasses are always an adequate substitute for a faceshield
explanation: The manual states a windshield is not a substitute for a faceshield or goggles -- most windshields will not protect your eyes from wind, and neither will eyeglasses or sunglasses, which also won't keep eyes from watering and might blow off.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.6, 'Eye and Face Protection'

question: To be effective, eye or faceshield protection must meet several requirements. Which of the following is one of them?
choice_a: It must be tinted at all times, day or night
choice_b: It must be free of scratches, resistant to penetration, and fasten securely so it does not blow off
choice_c: It should fit loosely so it can be removed quickly
choice_d: It only needs to cover one eye adequately
explanation: The manual lists several requirements for effective eye/faceshield protection, including being free of scratches, resistant to penetration, giving a clear view to either side, and fastening securely so it does not blow off.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.6, 'Eye and Face Protection'

question: When should tinted eye protection NOT be worn, according to the manual?
choice_b: Tinted eye protection should never be worn under any circumstance
choice_c: When little light is available, such as at dusk or night
choice_d: Tinted eye protection has no restrictions on when it is worn
explanation: The manual specifically warns that tinted eye protection should not be worn when little light is available, such as at dusk, night, or in poor weather.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.6, 'Eye and Face Protection'

question: What does the manual recommend about wearing a jacket even in warm weather?
choice_a: Jackets should never be worn in warm weather because they cause overheating
choice_b: A jacket is optional in all weather since pants provide equivalent protection
choice_c: Jackets are only needed in temperatures below 50 degrees
choice_d: Wear a jacket even in warm weather to prevent dehydration, since many are designed to protect without overheating the rider
explanation: The manual advises wearing a jacket even in warm weather to prevent dehydration, noting that many jackets are designed to protect without overheating the rider, even on summer days.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.6, 'Clothing'

question: What material does the manual say offers the most protection for a motorcycle jacket and pants?
choice_a: Leather, though sturdy synthetic material also provides a lot of protection
choice_d: Thin, loose-fitting fabric that flaps freely
explanation: The manual states that leather offers the most protection for jackets and pants, while sturdy synthetic material also provides a lot of protection.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.6, 'Clothing'

question: What does the manual recommend regarding boots or shoes for riding?
choice_a: Any lightweight sandal is acceptable as long as it is comfortable
choice_b: High and sturdy enough to cover the ankles, with hard, durable, slip-resistant soles and short heels, with laces tucked in
choice_c: Tall heels are preferred because they grip footrests better
choice_d: Loose, untied laces are fine as long as the boot fits well
explanation: The manual recommends boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support the ankles, with hard, durable, slip-resistant soles, short heels so they don't catch on rough surfaces, and laces tucked in so they won't catch on the motorcycle.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.6, 'Clothing'

question: What material does the manual recommend for gloves, and why?
choice_a: Thin cotton, because it allows maximum feel of the controls
choice_b: Gloves are discouraged because they reduce throttle control
choice_c: Leather or similar durable material, because gloves allow a better grip and help protect the hands in a crash
choice_d: Any material is equally protective as long as the gloves are stylish
explanation: The manual recommends gloves made of leather or similar durable material, noting that gloves allow a better grip and help protect the hands in a crash.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.7, 'Clothing'

question: Why does the manual say hearing protection is important, even for riders wearing a full-face helmet?
choice_a: Hearing protection is only cosmetic and has no real safety benefit
choice_b: A full-face helmet already blocks all engine and wind noise completely
choice_c: Hearing protection is illegal in most states, so it should be avoided
choice_d: Long-term exposure to engine and wind noise can cause permanent hearing damage even if a full-face helmet is worn
explanation: The manual explains that long-term exposure to engine and wind noise can cause permanent hearing damage even if a rider wears a full-face helmet, which is why hearing protection is recommended while still allowing important sounds like horns or sirens to be heard.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.7, 'Clothing'

question: What does the manual say about riding for long periods in cold weather?
choice_a: It can cause severe chill and fatigue, and a rider cannot control a motorcycle well when numb
choice_b: Cold weather has no effect on riding ability
choice_c: Riding in the cold actually sharpens a rider's reflexes
choice_d: Only the hands are affected by cold weather riding
explanation: The manual warns that riding for long periods in cold weather can cause severe chill and fatigue, and that a rider cannot control a motorcycle well while numb from the cold.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.7, 'Clothing'
